sections.heading: Lead
Background and recording
sections.wikitext:
"Hurts So Good" was written by John Mellencamp and [[George Green (songwriter)|George Green]], Mellencamp's childhood friend and occasional writing partner. The song was first conceived, Mellencamp claims, when he had uttered the phrase "hurt so good.” Mellencamp repeated the lines to Green, and they finished the song very quickly.<ref name="notes2">{{cite AV media notes |title=The Best That I Could Do 1978–1988 |others=John Mellencamp |year=1997 |chapter=Who's to Say the Way a Man Should Spend His Days: The First Two Hundred Years of the John Mellencamp Story |first=Timothy |last=White |author-link=Timothy White (editor) |page=6 |type=CD liner |publisher=Mercury Records |id= 314 536 738-2 |location=US }}</ref> In 2004, Mellencamp expounded on the writing of "Hurts So Good" in an interview with ''[[American Songwriter]]'' magazine: "George Green and I wrote that together. We exchanged lines back and forth between each other and laughed about it at the time. Then I went and picked up the guitar, and within seconds, I had those chords."<ref name="American Songwriter">{{cite interview| first= John | last= Mellencamp| interviewer= Paul Zollo |url= https://americansongwriter.com/2005/01/john-mellencamp/|title= John Mellencamp | work= American Songwriter | date=January 1, 2005}}</ref>

The song was recorded at [[Cherokee Studios]] in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]] and was [[Audio engineering|engineered]] by [[Don Gehman]] and George Tutko. Backing Mellencamp were [[Larry Crane (guitarist)|Larry Crane]] and Mike Wanchic ([[guitar]]s, [[Backing vocalist|backing vocals]]), [[Kenny Aronoff]] ([[Drum kit|drum]]s), [[George "Chocolate" Perry]] ([[Bass guitar|bass]]), and Dave Parman (backing vocals).<ref name="notes1" />
sections.text:
"Hurts So Good" was written by John Mellencamp and George Green, Mellencamp's childhood friend and occasional writing partner. The song was first conceived, Mellencamp claims, when he had uttered the phrase "hurt so good.” Mellencamp repeated the lines to Green, and they finished the song very quickly. In 2004, Mellencamp expounded on the writing of "Hurts So Good" in an interview with American Songwriter magazine: "George Green and I wrote that together. We exchanged lines back and forth between each other and laughed about it at the time. Then I went and picked up the guitar, and within seconds, I had those chords."

The song was recorded at Cherokee Studios in Los Angeles, California and was engineered by Don Gehman and George Tutko. Backing Mellencamp were Larry Crane and Mike Wanchic (guitars, backing vocals), Kenny Aronoff (drums), George "Chocolate" Perry (bass), and Dave Parman (backing vocals).
